target: Se eu tivesse começado antes, já teria terminado.
english: If I had started earlier, I'd already be done.
tip: For past regrets, pair tivesse plus participle (começado) with teria plus participle (terminado): if I had, I would have.

target: Se a gente tivesse um quintal, plantaria uma horta.
english: If we had a backyard, we'd plant a garden.
tip: A gente means we in casual speech but takes singular verbs, so tivesse and plantaria, never the nós forms.

target: Aqui se fala português.
english: Portuguese is spoken here.
tip: se fala means 'is spoken'; the se makes the verb passive with no separate word for 'is': aqui se fala.

target: Eu lhe dei o recado.
english: I gave him/her the message.
tip: Lhe is the indirect object pronoun, to him or to her. Eu lhe dei o recado = I gave the message to him or her.

target: A casa foi reformada recentemente.
english: The house was recently renovated.
tip: In passive voice the participle agrees with the subject. Casa is feminine, so it is reformada, not reformado.

target: É proibido fumar neste recinto.
english: Smoking is prohibited in this area.
tip: Before an infinitive, é proibido stays invariable: é proibido fumar. It agrees only when a noun follows, as in proibida a entrada.

target: Tampouco ele sabia da reunião.
english: He didn't know about the meeting either.
tip: Tampouco means not either, the negative of também. Tampouco ele sabia = he did not know either. It is a touch more formal than também não.

target: A conta foi paga pela empresa.
english: The bill was paid by the company.
tip: In the passive, the agent that did the action follows por. A conta foi paga pela empresa = the bill was paid by the company.

target: Se ele não fosse tão orgulhoso, pediria desculpas.
english: If he weren't so proud, he'd apologize.
tip: For an unreal present situation, use se plus imperfect subjunctive then the conditional: se ele não fosse orgulhoso, pediria desculpas.

target: O médico recomendou que ele tomasse mais água.
english: The doctor recommended he drink more water.
tip: Recommendation verbs force the past subjunctive: recomendou que tomasse, where English just says 'he drink'.

target: Embora esteja frio, vou sair de camiseta.
english: Although it's cold, I'm going out in a t-shirt.
tip: Embora, meaning although, always takes the subjunctive: embora esteja frio, never embora está frio.

target: O pai disse ao filho que precisava estudar mais.
english: The father told his son he needed to study more.
tip: disse que is the standard way to report speech; casual Brazilian talk often swaps in falou que.

target: Quanto mais estudo, mais percebo que não sei nada.
english: The more I study, the more I realize I know nothing.
tip: 'Quanto mais... mais' = 'the more... the more'.

target: Aluga-se sala comercial.
english: Commercial office to rent.
tip: Aluga-se uses passive se, so the verb agrees with its noun; the plural would be Alugam-se salas.

target: Pare de fazer barulho, por favor.
english: Stop making noise, please.
tip: 'Parar de' + infinitive = to stop doing something.

target: Ele viajou apesar de estar doente.
english: He traveled despite being sick.
tip: Apesar de means despite and is followed by an infinitive, as in apesar de estar doente.

target: Ela deixou de fumar há dois anos.
english: She quit smoking two years ago.
tip: 'Deixar de' + infinitive = to stop/quit doing something.

target: Acabei de ler um livro incrível.
english: I just read an incredible book.
tip: Acabar de plus an infinitive means to have just done something: acabei de ler = I just read.

target: Assim que eu chegar, te ligo.
english: As soon as I arrive, I'll call you.
tip: Assim que, meaning as soon as, takes the future subjunctive: assim que eu chegar = when I arrive.

target: Ela anda comendo muito fast food.
english: She's been eating a lot of fast food.
tip: Andar plus a gerund describes a recent ongoing habit: anda comendo = she's been eating lately.

target: Diz-se que ele vai se candidatar.
english: It's said that he's going to run for office.
tip: 'Diz-se que' – impersonal way to express hearsay/rumor.

target: Até onde eu sei, o projeto foi aprovado.
english: As far as I know, the project was approved.
tip: 'Até onde eu sei' + indicative – states speaker's knowledge.

target: Uma vez que a decisão foi tomada, não há como voltar atrás.
english: Once the decision has been made, there's no going back.
tip: uma vez que looks like 'one time that' but means 'once' or 'given that'; it isn't counting times.

target: Desde que eu me lembro, ele sempre foi assim.
english: As far as I can remember, he's always been like that.
tip: 'Desde que' can mean 'since' (time) or 'as long as' (condition).

target: Acabamos de receber a notícia.
english: We just received the news.
tip: Acabar de plus infinitive means to have just done something. Acabamos de receber = we have just received, a very recent past.

target: Eles andam brigando muito ultimamente.
english: They've been fighting a lot lately.
tip: Andar plus gerund describes a recent ongoing tendency. Eles andam brigando = they have been fighting lately, not literally walking.

target: Nem por isso deixei de tentar.
english: That didn't stop me from trying.
tip: Deixar de plus infinitive means to stop or give up doing something. Deixei de tentar = I stopped trying.

target: À medida que envelhecemos, ficamos mais sábios.
english: As we age, we become wiser.
tip: à medida que is the proportional 'as', the more X the more Y; it isn't the 'like' meaning of como.

target: Ele tornou a ligar no dia seguinte.
english: He called again the next day.
tip: 'Tornar a' + infinitive = to do something again – formal.

target: Ou seja, a reunião foi cancelada.
english: In other words, the meeting was canceled.
tip: ou seja is literally 'or be it', with seja the subjunctive of ser, frozen into the phrase 'in other words'.
